items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The diff is the same as the reference. The names say what they do (compile_json_path_final_key, HasKeyOrArrayIndex), a short comment explains why the final key goes through json.dumps, and the formatting matches the existing code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It adds one overridable hook and a two-line subclass, reuses compile_json_path for the leading segments, and leaves no per-backend copies of the path logic, dead code or debug output.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: json.dumps escapes the key properly and no exception handling is needed. The agent checked SQLite path behaviour by hand (e.g. $[1]."2") and the hidden tests pass (F2P 2/2, P2P 78/78).

items.name: Array-index semantics kept for isnull / exact=None paths
items.name_zh: isnull / exact=None 路径保留数组下标语义
items.evidence: The final has_key key goes through json.dumps in the shared as_sql used by SQLite, MySQL and Oracle. HasKeyOrArrayIndex is used in KeyTransformIsNull.as_sqlite/as_oracle and KeyTransformExact.as_oracle, so array indices still work there. Intermediate path segments are unchanged.
